theory.overview: Searching is the process of finding a specific element within a data structure. The choice of search algorithm depends on data organization: linear search works on unsorted data ($O(n)$), binary search requires sorted data ($O(\log n)$). Binary search is one of the most important algorithms—repeatedly halving the search space. Variations include searching in rotated sorted arrays, finding first/last occurrence, and searching in 2D matrices. This chapter covers linear search, binary search, and their variants with practical applications.

sections.title: Linear Search
sections.content: Linear search scans through elements sequentially until target found or end reached. Time complexity: $O(n)$ best/average/worst. Space: $O(1)$. Simple and works on unsorted data. Used when data is small, unsorted, or when searching for multiple occurrences. Can be optimized with sentinel (place target at end to avoid bounds check) or with early exit conditions.

sections.title: Binary Search
sections.content: Binary search works on sorted arrays. Compare target with middle element. If equal, return index. If target < middle, search left half. If target > middle, search right half. Repeat until found or search space exhausted. Time: $O(\log n)$ comparisons. Space: $O(1)$ iterative, $O(\log n)$ recursive. Key insight: each comparison halves search space.
sections.algorithm: low=0, high=n-1. While low≤high: mid=(low+high)//2. If arr[mid]==target: return mid. If target<arr[mid]: high=mid-1. Else: low=mid+1. Return -1.

sections.title: Binary Search Variants
sections.content: Finding first occurrence: when arr[mid]==target, continue searching left (high=mid-1) to find earlier occurrence. Finding last occurrence: when arr[mid]==target, continue searching right (low=mid+1). Finding insertion position: return low when loop ends (position where target would be inserted). These variants are essential for problems with duplicates.

variants.name: First occurrence
variants.modification: When found, high=mid-1 to search left

variants.name: Last occurrence
variants.modification: When found, low=mid+1 to search right

sections.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
sections.content: Rotated sorted array: [4,5,6,7,0,1,2] (sorted then rotated). Binary search still works but need to determine which half is sorted. If arr[low] ≤ arr[mid], left half is sorted. Check if target in left half range. Else search right. Similar logic for right half sorted. Time: $O(\log n)$.
sections.logic: Determine sorted half by comparing arr[low] and arr[mid]. Check if target in sorted half range. Narrow search accordingly.

sections.title: Search in 2D Matrix
sections.content: For matrix sorted row-wise and column-wise, start from top-right corner. If target > current, move down (all values in current row are smaller). If target < current, move left (all values in current column are larger). Time: $O(m+n)$. For fully sorted matrix (each row sorted, first element of each row > last of previous), treat as 1D sorted array with binary search.

approaches.method: Start top-right, move down or left

keyConcepts.name: Search Space Reduction
keyConcepts.description: Binary search reduces search space by half each iteration. $n \rightarrow n/2 \rightarrow n/4 \rightarrow ... \rightarrow 1$. Total iterations: $\log_2 n$.
keyConcepts.formula: After k iterations: search space = $n / 2^k$. When $n / 2^k = 1$, $k = \log_2 n$

keyConcepts.name: Mid Calculation
keyConcepts.description: mid = (low + high) // 2 can overflow for large values. Use mid = low + (high - low) // 2 to prevent overflow.

keyConcepts.name: Termination Condition
keyConcepts.description: Loop while low ≤ high. When low > high, search space empty. Return low for insertion position (where target would go).
keyConcepts.invariant: Target always in [low, high] if it exists

keyConcepts.name: Duplicate Handling
keyConcepts.description: For first/last occurrence, don't return immediately when found. Continue searching in one direction to find boundary.
keyConcepts.pattern: First: search left after finding. Last: search right after finding

steps.title: Calculate Mid
steps.description: mid = low + (high - low) // 2 to avoid overflow.

steps.title: Compare
steps.description: Compare arr[mid] with target. If equal, return mid.

steps.title: Narrow Search
steps.description: If target < arr[mid], high = mid - 1. Else low = mid + 1.
steps.code: if target < arr[mid]: high = mid - 1; else: low = mid + 1;

steps.title: Repeat or Return
steps.description: Repeat until low > high. Return -1 if not found.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Search
practiceProblems.description: Implement binary search on sorted array. Return index of target or -1.
practiceProblems.solution: Standard binary search. low=0, high=n-1. While low≤high: mid=(low+high)//2. Compare and narrow. Return index or -1.

practiceProblems.title: Search Insert Position
practiceProblems.description: Find index where target would be inserted to maintain sorted order.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. When loop ends (low > high), return low (insertion position).

practiceProblems.title: First Bad Version
practiceProblems.description: Find first bad version where isBadVersion(n) returns true for all n >= first bad.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on version numbers. If isBadVersion(mid), search left (first bad could be earlier). Else search right.
hints: If bad, search left for first

practiceProblems.title: Search in Rotated Array
practiceProblems.description: Search target in rotated sorted array (no duplicates).
practiceProblems.solution: Determine which half is sorted. Check if target in sorted half. Narrow search accordingly.
hints: Check if left half sorted: arr[low] ≤ arr[mid]
If target in sorted range, search there

practiceProblems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Array
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum element in rotated sorted array (no duplicates).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. If arr[mid] > arr[high], min is in right half. Else min is in left half (including mid).
hints: If arr[mid] > arr[high], min in right

practiceProblems.title: Find Peak Element
practiceProblems.description: Find peak element (greater than neighbors). Array may have multiple peaks.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. If arr[mid] < arr[mid+1], peak is in right half. Else peak is in left half (including mid).
hints: Else go left (mid could be peak)

practiceProblems.title: Search a 2D Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Search target in matrix where each row sorted, first of each row > last of previous.
practiceProblems.solution: Treat as 1D sorted array. Binary search on index 0 to m*n-1. Convert index to (row, col): row = index // n, col = index % n.
hints: Binary search on index 0 to m*n-1

practiceProblems.title: Search 2D Matrix II
practiceProblems.description: Search target in matrix sorted row-wise and column-wise.
practiceProblems.solution: Start from top-right. If target > current, move down. If target < current, move left. Continue until found or out of bounds.

practiceProblems.title: Find First and Last Position
practiceProblems.description: Find first and last position of target in sorted array with duplicates.
practiceProblems.solution: Two binary searches. First: when found, continue left (high=mid-1). Last: when found, continue right (low=mid+1).

practiceProblems.title: Single Element in Sorted Array
practiceProblems.description: Find single element in sorted array where all others appear twice.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on even indices. If arr[mid] == arr[mid+1], single is on right. Else single is on left.
hints: Single is at even index before pair

practiceProblems.title: Guess Number Higher or Lower
practiceProblems.description: Guess number between 1 and n. API tells if guess is higher, lower, or correct.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. If guess(target) returns -1 (too high), search lower. If 1 (too low), search higher.

practiceProblems.title: H-Index II
practiceProblems.description: Find h-index given sorted citations array (citations[i] >= n-i means h-index >= n-i).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. Find largest n-i where citations[i] >= n-i. Return n-i.
hints: Binary search for largest valid n-i

practiceProblems.title: Capacity To Ship Packages
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum capacity to ship all weights within D days (must ship in order).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on capacity (low=max weight, high=sum). Check if can ship within D days with given capacity.

practiceProblems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum eating speed (bananas/hour) to finish all piles in H hours.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on speed (low=1, high=max pile). Calculate hours needed for each speed. Find minimum feasible speed.
hints: Find minimum speed where hours ≤ H

practiceProblems.title: Split Array Largest Sum
practiceProblems.description: Split array into m subarrays to minimize largest sum among subarrays.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on max sum (low=max element, high=sum). Check if can split into ≤ m subarrays with max sum ≤ mid.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
practiceProblems.description: Find minimal length subarray with sum ≥ target (positive numbers only).
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window. Expand right, add to sum. When sum ≥ target, shrink left while maintaining condition. Track min length.

practiceProblems.title: Find Smallest Letter
practiceProblems.description: Find smallest letter greater than target (wrap around if none).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. If letters[mid] > target, search left. Else search right. Return letters[low % n].

practiceProblems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
practiceProblems.description: Find median of two sorted arrays (combined).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on smaller array. Find partition such that elements on left ≤ elements on right. Calculate median from boundary elements.

practiceProblems.title: Search in Rotated Array II
practiceProblems.description: Search target in rotated sorted array with duplicates.
practiceProblems.solution: Similar to no-duplicate case, but when arr[low] == arr[mid] == arr[high], can't determine sorted half. Increment low, decrement high.
hints: Increment low, decrement high in this case

practiceProblems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Array II
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum in rotated sorted array with duplicates.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search. If arr[mid] > arr[high], min in right. If arr[mid] < arr[high], min in left. If equal, decrement high.

practiceProblems.title: Pow(x, n)
practiceProblems.description: Calculate x^n efficiently.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary exponentiation. x^n = (x^(n/2))^2 if n even, = x * x^(n-1) if n odd. Handle negative n.
hints: n even: square result of n/2

practiceProblems.title: Sqrt(x)
practiceProblems.description: Find integer square root of x (floor of sqrt).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on [0, x]. If mid*mid == x, return mid. If mid*mid < x, search right. Else search left.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Perfect Square
practiceProblems.description: Check if number is perfect square.
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on [1, n/2]. Check if mid*mid == n. Or use math: n == int(sqrt(n))^2.

practiceProblems.title: Find Right Interval
practiceProblems.description: For each interval, find right interval (start ≥ current end) with smallest start.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort intervals by start, store original indices. For each interval, binary search for smallest start ≥ its end.
hints: Sort by start, track original indices
Binary search for each interval's end

practiceProblems.title: Arranging Coins
practiceProblems.description: Find number of complete rows of coins in staircase (k rows need k(k+1)/2 coins).
practiceProblems.solution: Binary search on number of rows. Check if k(k+1)/2 ≤ n. Find maximum k satisfying this.

minigame.description: Guess the number using binary search! Fewer guesses = higher score.
